items.summary: We prove that a finite poset with at most fifteen elements, width at most three, and the following common-incomparability property has at most 48 antichains: for every x < y, the elements incomparable with both x and y form a chain of size at most two. An explicit fifteen-element poset attains the bound. We show that order-six stable-marriage rotation posets satisfy these hypotheses by examining convex rotation blocks and their fixed partner pools. This gives a structural upper bound of 48 stable matchings, matching the lower bound already provided by Benjamin, Converse, and Krieger in 1995. Equality forces fifteen rotations, all of size two, and every one of the 36 man–woman pairs occurs in some stable matching. Provenance note: This preprint is accompanied by reproducible verification artifacts and a partial Lean formalization. The Lean development verifies the finite-poset core and supporting components; it does not formalize the entire stable-marriage theorem f(6) = 48 end to end. The source-code and reproducibility repository is available at https://github.com/insammael/stable-marriage-f6 and is linked as a related resource.
items.title: Small Rotation Blocks and the Order-Six Stable Marriage Problem

items.summary: Abstract Distributed version control preserves source states, ancestry, branching, merging, and collaboration with extraordinary success. It does not ordinarily require engineering intent, failed approaches, claim scope, verification evidence, residual disagreement, or continuation state to exist as typed repository objects. Those records instead tend to be distributed across commit prose, review systems, issue trackers, CI logs, artifact stores, chat, and human memory. This disclosure explores a broader version-control model for software developed by humans and agents without claiming that content addressing, provenance, attestations, change-oriented versioning, or agent memory are new in isolation. Gemel models an evidence-bearing change : a content-addressed relation from an exact input state to an exact output state, linked to intent, operations, producer provenance, claims, evidence, residuals, verification scope, and causal context. Trajectories preserve completed, rejected, interrupted, superseded, and inconclusive work. Claims remain declarations rather than stored truth; support and readiness are derived conservatively from evidence, residuals, freshness, supersession, and policy. Context manifests and checkpoints provide bounded continuation surfaces without requiring private reasoning transcripts. The inspected Rust reference implementation defines deterministic canonical encoding, BLAKE3-256 identities, immutable objects, mutable refs, rebuildable indexes, 24 object families, Git-carried exchange, deterministic Git projection, semantic indexing, native and hosted synchronization, agent queries, policy checks, and an FRF court runner. For this paper, the supplied source archive was independently built in a clean temporary directory and cargo test --all-targets completed 236 tests with zero failures. This result is implementation-specific conformance evidence. It is not evidence that Gemel improves developer productivity, agent reliability, or industrial outcomes. Gemel composes with the Forensic Residual Framework (FRF) as an evidence plane and with FRF-Fuzz as a discovery plane. The paper situates that composition against Git facilities, patch algebra, provenance models, software-supply-chain attestations, reproducible builds, software archives, event sourcing, rationale capture, and agent memory. It discloses alternative embodiments and defines falsifiable evaluations for handoff quality, repeated-error reduction, evidence freshness, reconciliation, interoperability, context cost, storage overhead, and longitudinal fuzzing. Its principal claim is architectural: software history can be represented as an engineering graph in which source state, intent, evidence, residual uncertainty, negative knowledge, and continuation state possess explicit identity and scope. Whether that representation earns its operational cost remains an empirical question. Keywords distributed version control; Git; agentic software development; evidence engineering; provenance; content addressing; Merkle DAG; software agents; developmental trajectories; negative knowledge; residual primacy; FRF; FRF-Fuzz; reproducibility; software archaeology; semantic lineage; source provenance; event sourcing.

items.summary: Research and educational instrument. Not for clinical use, for the care of any patient, or to determine or influence any drug dose. A simulation-calibrated informatics pipeline that fits a single-compartment exponential approximation to published population pharmacokinetic models of unfractionated heparin during cardiopulmonary bypass, and renders the result as an institution-specific decay nomogram. This is the supporting code and archived analysis for manuscript JCVA-D-26-01511. Published models of heparin disposition are biexponential and require a computer to evaluate. The pipeline asks how well a single decay constant k — calibrated to an institution's own dosing, weight and bypass-time distributions — can approximate a chosen reference model, and quantifies where it fails. The answer differs sharply by model: at the reversal timepoint the approximation holds to 0.38% mean absolute error for Lanoiselée and 0.44% for Jia, but to 10.3% for Delavenne, rising to 72% after repeated supplemental boluses. Contents. Five reference-model implementations with their published parameters and provenance; seeded cohort sampling and calibration; agreement statistics; nomogram geometry and rendering; a Streamlit dashboard; an automated test suite; and a frozen analysis run comprising 20 result tables, the main-text and supplementary figures, a run manifest and a manuscript-ready summary. A sixth model (PRODOSE-2) is implemented and tested but withheld from the active pipeline pending validation and peer review. Reproduction. Every reported number regenerates from one seeded command: pip install -r requirements-frozen.txt python run_analysis.py --seed 20260912 --outdir /tmp/check python check_frozen.py /tmp/check All randomness comes from explicitly seeded generators, each analysis stage drawing from its own independent stream. Re-running reproduces every archived result to within floating-point rounding on any machine, and byte-for-byte on the machine the archive was built on. The manifest records the seed, the commit, the package versions and every analysis decision. Continuous integration runs the suite on two Python versions, each test file again in isolation, and the reproduction check on every push. Verification, and its limits. Automated checks confirm that each closed-form solution actually solves its own differential equations and satisfies the identities they imply, and six landmark values from a published simulation are reproduced to within 3%. No participant-level data from any source study is held, so no model is re-fitted and no prediction is compared with an observation. What is demonstrated is faithful implementation of the published models — not that the published models are correct. No external or predictive validation is claimed. Scope. The pipeline represents the pharmacokinetic central-compartment amount only. It does not model the pharmacodynamic layer — anti-factor Xa activity or activated clotting time — nor peripheral-compartment heparin, antithrombin, protamine pharmacology or heparin rebound. Converting a residual amount into a protamine dose requires an institutional ratio that this software does not supply. Intended purpose. This software is a research and educational instrument whose purpose is to demonstrate and teach an informatics method under simulated conditions. Within that intended purpose it is not a medical device. items.summary: This work presents reusable mathematical bridges extracted from the Chronos formal-verification programme and related Lean developments in constrained dynamics, quantum mechanics, gravity, operator theory, partial differential equations, and Yang–Mills theory.   The purpose of the work is to make formally developed mathematical structures available for reuse beyond the physical problems in which they were originally constructed.   The paper develops four primary reusable connections.   First, it presents an internal-time framework for constrained Hamiltonian systems. When a candidate clock has a nonvanishing rate along a constrained trajectory, the system can be reparameterized with respect to that clock, producing relational evolution. This connects directly with the existing Chronos frozen-to-flow and Wheeler–DeWitt formalization.   Second, it develops a quantum–classical shared-time bridge based on expectation-value evolution. For suitable Hamiltonians, including the constant-force system already treated in the formal programme, quantum expectation values obey exact classical equations of motion.   Third, it extracts a reusable operator-theoretic chain connecting coercive lower bounds to positive spectral bounds, invertibility, and quantitative inverse or resolvent control. Together with cutoff and graph-core machinery developed during the Yang–Mills formalization, this provides reusable infrastructure for unbounded operators in quantum mechanics and partial differential equations.   Fourth, it presents the general inverse-distance field structure underlying the existing Chronos gravity formalization. A radial inverse-distance potential produces an inverse-square gradient, satisfies the three-dimensional vacuum Laplace equation away from the source, and has radius-independent spherical flux. The same mathematical structure can therefore be instantiated in Newtonian gravity, electrostatics, Green-function theory, and other potential problems.   The central goal is compositional reuse. Rather than treating each formal proof as an isolated endpoint, the work identifies intermediate machine-checkable theorem structures that can serve as starting points for additional formal developments.   Immediate applications include relational clock models, Wheeler–DeWitt and constrained systems, Ehrenfest and semiclassical quantum dynamics, electrostatic inverse-square fields, Schrödinger operators, spectral-gap arguments, elliptic PDEs, gauge systems, and other operator-theoretic problems.   This paper accompanies the broader Chronos formal-verification programme and is intended as an openly reusable mathematical and formal-physics resource.
items.title: Reusable Formal Bridges from Chronos Verification: Internal Time, Quantum–Classical Dynamics, Operator Control, and Inverse-Distance Fields

items.summary: We investigate Floquet--spin-orbit compensation in the three-band $α$-$T_3$ system, which interpolates between graphene at $α=0$ and the dice lattice at $α=1$. By tuning the interplay between an off-resonant circularly polarized optical field and intrinsic spin--orbit coupling, we identify three distinct pairwise band-degeneracy conditions in the quasienergy spectrum: (i) valley--spin degeneracy, (ii) spin--band degeneracy, and (iii) flat--dispersive band degeneracy. The flat band is not an artifact of a two-band reduction but rather an exact property of the continuum Hamiltonian at this compensation point, where the complete three-band Hamiltonian supports a momentum-independent dark state. A winding-two low-energy Hamiltonian and a finite-momentum Berry-curvature maximum, whose radius scales as the square root of the detuning, emerge from detuning this contact. We further show that the intrinsic transverse thermoelectric response encodes these spectrum patterns. The flat- and quadratic-band degeneracy can be predicted for $0<α<1/2$ because the two response scales linked to the linear contacts have a monotonic ratio independent of the common spin--orbit energy scale. This allows an inverse determination of $α$ and of the common spectral scale. The analytical results are confirmed by full three-band Kubo calculations, which also define the regime in which this inverse characterization is still observable. These results connect an experimentally accessible, Berry-curvature-sensitive thermoelectric response to tunable Floquet--spin--orbit band geometry.
items.title: Floquet-spin-orbit compensation and flat- and quadratic-band contact in the $α$-$T_3$ lattice

items.summary: We present an HTTP threat detection system embedded in a production reverse proxy that achieves sub-500ns per-request inference latency. The system combines a depth-limited CART decision tree with a compact two-layer MLP in an ensemble architecture, where the tree provides fast-path classification and the MLP refines uncertain cases. Model weights are exported as Rust `const` arrays, enabling zero-allocation deployment with no runtime deserialization. We formalize structural safety properties of the ensemble in the Lean~4 theorem prover, establishing a three-tier verification approach covering structural invariants, weight-dependent decision bounds, and floating-point error propagation. In initial small-scale trials on a combined dataset of production logs, CSIC-2010, and CIC-IDS2017-derived features, the ensemble achieves >99% validation accuracy for both scanner and DDoS detection, with tree inference completing in under 2ns and full ensemble inference under 6ns. We discuss limitations of the current training data and outline directions for scaling to larger, human-labeled corpora.
items.title: Sub-Microsecond HTTP Threat Detection with Decision Tree–MLP Ensembles and Lean 4 Verification

items.summary: Large language models can hold knowledge they do not report. A model may sandbag on a capability evaluation, or answer against what it internally knows, and its outputs alone cannot tell whether it is hiding an answer or simply does not have one. We borrow the Concealed Information Test, a forensic method that identifies guilty knowledge by presenting a suspect with the true detail among plausible decoys and measuring a stronger response to the item they recognize. Our method, Probe of Internal Recognition (PIR), does the same inside a model. It presents a question with its candidate answers and reads, from the model's internal states, which candidate the model recognizes as correct. PIR is reference-free, needing no honest reference model and no labeled truth corpus. Across eight models from five families (Gemma, Qwen, Llama, Mistral, and Phi), PIR recovers the recognized answer at 0.70 to 0.87 balanced accuracy, well above the 0.28 to 0.40 unknown-item baseline and the 0.25 chance rate. It stays readable across every form of concealment we test, from prompted deception and trained sandbagging to external password-locked and circuit-broken checkpoints, with recognition between 0.85 and 0.93. When the model hides a known answer, recognition stays high. When unlearning removes the knowledge, recognition drops to the level of a question the model never knew. PIR therefore separates a model that will not answer from one that cannot, which supports sandbagging audits and unlearning verification. The signal is causal, adds information beyond black-box behavioral cues, and extends from multiple-choice questions to free-form generation.
items.title: A Lie Detector Test for Language Models: Reading Knowledge a Model Won't Reveal

items.summary: Anticoncentration is a key ingredient in complexity theoretic arguments for quantum advantage from Gaussian boson sampling. Here we prove polynomial small ball anticoncentration for complex Gaussian transpose Gram hafnians and complex symmetric Gaussian hafnians. For a k × 2n matrix X with independent standard complex Gaussian entries, we establish polynomial small ball anticoncentration for haf(XᵀX) under k ≥ 4n and n²/k = O(log n). For hafnians of 2n × 2n complex symmetric Gaussian matrices, polynomial small ball anticoncentration holds for every n ≥ 1. In both ensembles, any prescribed inverse polynomial failure probability can be achieved with an inverse polynomial small ball radius, uniformly over all centers. These results go beyond moment based anticoncentration by controlling the probability of small hafnian amplitudes. The proof combines Fourier compression with conditional Wishart geometry to handle dependent hafnian cofactors. Files: main.pdf contains the main article (14 pages); supplement.pdf contains the supplementary proofs and additional results (33 pages). Related Lean verification sources: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22554594 and https://github.com/HongruZhao/ComplexGramHafnians.
items.title: Local Anticoncentration for Gaussian Boson Sampling via Conditional Wishart Geometry

items.summary: Split-Zero cohomology and the zeta-function research programme is a cumulative collection of mathematical papers, complete LaTeX proofs, formalization sources, calculations and literature-based research notes. Its central question is how the zeros of the Riemann zeta function can be studied through explicitly constructed arithmetic cohomology, spectral actions and quantitative metric estimates. The collection also retains the related heat-flow, arithmetic-trace, fluid, complexity and thermal-geometry investigations from which parts of this programme developed. Project and reading guide · Research contents · Machine-readable workbench index . Papers remain separate readable PDFs; the source archives supply the corresponding editable mathematics and supporting materials. What the collection contains Split-Zero coefficients, geometry and cohomology. The construction retains a ring's internal zero and a separate symbol for absence, so a zero element in a specified support fibre is not confused with an absent fibre. The papers construct coefficient maps, quotients, homology, finite spectral jets and their relation to the infinite theta quotient. Deligne's Weil II provides a motivating source for the cohomology–duality–weight-control programme; its finite-field theorem is not asserted to apply automatically to the Riemann zeta function. Read the cohomology and weight-control paper and the foundational objects and maps . Arithmetic theta sources and analytic control. The central analytic complex is [V → B], with theta map Θ and quotient B/ΘV. Scaling acts by D = −x∂x; the Mellin-side arithmetic function is 2ξ(s), where ξ is the completed Riemann zeta function. The papers carry finite zero packets, including multiplicities, through the original source maps and least-norm quotient metrics. They develop source recovery, residue and period maps, tensor and exterior constructions, Mellin and Gamma estimates, orthogonal-polynomial kernels, Hankel–Toda determinant identities, boundary terms, and growing-degree volume and covariance calculations. The cumulative Split-Zero reader , its proof companion , and the separate kernel, conductor and source-transport papers retain the complete arguments. Conductor geometry and spectral observation. Further papers calculate the original relation and conductor maps, kernels, quotient volumes, real-period resonances, inverse spectra and finite observation bounds. The native spectral paper , real-period paper , resonance-direction paper and inverse-power observation paper have distinct, explicit scopes. Geometric examples are not represented as identified arithmetic zeta-zero packets. Formalization and reproducible calculation. The Lean sources and formalization notes cover specified algebraic, quotient and homological interfaces. Source packages retain exact finite checkers, numerical or interval calculations where supplied, figures, manifests and verification records. A Lean check of an interface, a finite algebra test and an analytic proof are documented as different forms of evidence; none silently certifies the others. The wider zeta literature and connected investigations. The separate zeta reader , fluid/Navier–Stokes reader , de Bruijn–Newman heat-flow reader , Connes/arithmetic-trace reader , geometric-complexity reader and vacuum and thermal-geometry reader preserve the earlier research routes and their stated limitations. Related Unified Flow calculations concern specified black-hole, thermal, spectral-zeta and geometric-flow probes. The CUE research map connects existing random-unitary-matrix, Mellin and finite-phase-space work. An analogy or proposed connection is not presented as an established implication between major conjectures. How to read and assess the work This is an ongoing research programme, not a claimed proof or disproof of RH or the other major conjectures discussed in the connected notes. The remaining arithmetic estimates and identifications are stated in the individual paper
items.title: Split-Zero cohomology and the zeta-function research programme

items.summary: This release contains the SMT-LIB2 benchmarks accompanying our paper, "Invulnerability Checking for Memory Protection Extensions Against Meltdown." It includes 16 benchmarks covering load-store queue sizes of 8, 16, 32, and 64 entries. Each size includes a secure baseline and three MPX Trojan variants: Base, Bound, and Illegal Memory Access. A verification script runs the benchmarks using Z3, checks the results against the expected outcomes, and saves the solver output and execution times.
items.title: Supporting Code for Invulnerability Checking for Memory Protection Extensions Against Meltdown

items.summary: Preconditioned Total Field Inversion: a single-step method that inverts the total field directly to susceptibility over the whole field-of-view, jointly performing background-field removal and dipole inversion. Uses a preconditioner (χ = P·y, larger outside the brain) so the large out-of-brain background susceptibility is well-conditioned, with MEDI-style L1 morphology regularization. QSM-CI reconstruction method tfi-qsmrs . Browse and run it at https://qsmxt.github.io/QSM-CI/submission.html?method=tfi-qsmrs .
items.title: QSM-CI method: TFI (QSM.rs) (v4)

Rather than treating each formal proof as an isolated endpoint, the work identifies intermediate machine-checkable theorem structures that can serve as starting points for additional formal developments.   Immediate applications include relational clock models, Wheeler–DeWitt and constrained systems, Ehrenfest and semiclassical quantum dynamics, electrostatic inverse-square fields, Schrödinger operators, spectral-gap arguments, elliptic PDEs, gauge systems, and other operator-theoretic problems.   This paper accompanies the broader Chronos formal-verification programme and is intended as an openly reusable mathematical and formal-physics resource.
items.title: Reusable Formal Bridges from Chronos Verification: Internal Time, Quantum–Classical Dynamics, Operator Control, and Inverse-Distance Fields

items.summary: We investigate Floquet--spin-orbit compensation in the three-band $α$-$T_3$ system, which interpolates between graphene at $α=0$ and the dice lattice at $α=1$. By tuning the interplay between an off-resonant circularly polarized optical field and intrinsic spin--orbit coupling, we identify three distinct pairwise band-degeneracy conditions in the quasienergy spectrum: (i) valley--spin degeneracy, (ii) spin--band degeneracy, and (iii) flat--dispersive band degeneracy. The flat band is not an artifact of a two-band reduction but rather an exact property of the continuum Hamiltonian at this compensation point, where the complete three-band Hamiltonian supports a momentum-independent dark state. A winding-two low-energy Hamiltonian and a finite-momentum Berry-curvature maximum, whose radius scales as the square root of the detuning, emerge from detuning this contact. We further show that the intrinsic transverse thermoelectric response encodes these spectrum patterns. The flat- and quadratic-band degeneracy can be predicted for $0<α<1/2$ because the two response scales linked to the linear contacts have a monotonic ratio independent of the common spin--orbit energy scale. This allows an inverse determination of $α$ and of the common spectral scale. The analytical results are confirmed by full three-band Kubo calculations, which also define the regime in which this inverse characterization is still observable. These results connect an experimentally accessible, Berry-curvature-sensitive thermoelectric response to tunable Floquet--spin--orbit band geometry.
items.title: Floquet-spin-orbit compensation and flat- and quadratic-band contact in the $α$-$T_3$ lattice

items.summary: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) have attracted extensive attention in recent years due to their strong capability for high-quality 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis from multi-view images. Existing methods usually rely on high-quality sharp inputs, while real-world image acquisition is highly susceptible to blur degradation, which severely affects the reconstruction quality of NeRF. In this paper, we propose a novel Mamba-driven world-state-aware adaptive deblurring neural radiance field, termed WS-NeRF, to address image degradation and 3D inconsistency. We formulate the alternating optimization of radiance fields as a dynamic evolution process with temporal memory, and jointly exploit comprehensive multi-dimensional world states and a mixture-of-experts mechanism to dynamically adjust the confidence of deblurring priors. Experimental results show that WS-NeRF significantly improves blurry radiance field reconstruction quality, achieving better performance on PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS, while exhibiting more stable iterative recovery behavior.
items.title: WS-NeRF: A Mamba-Driven World-State-Aware Adaptive Deblurring Neural Radiance Field

items.summary: Anticoncentration is a key ingredient in complexity theoretic arguments for quantum advantage from Gaussian boson sampling. Here we prove polynomial small ball anticoncentration for complex Gaussian transpose Gram hafnians and complex symmetric Gaussian hafnians. For a k × 2n matrix X with independent standard complex Gaussian entries, we establish polynomial small ball anticoncentration for haf(XᵀX) under k ≥ 4n and n²/k = O(log n). For hafnians of 2n × 2n complex symmetric Gaussian matrices, polynomial small ball anticoncentration holds for every n ≥ 1. In both ensembles, any prescribed inverse polynomial failure probability can be achieved with an inverse polynomial small ball radius, uniformly over all centers. These results go beyond moment based anticoncentration by controlling the probability of small hafnian amplitudes. The proof combines Fourier compression with conditional Wishart geometry to handle dependent hafnian cofactors. items.summary: We present an HTTP threat detection system embedded in a production reverse proxy that achieves sub-500ns per-request inference latency. The system combines a depth-limited CART decision tree with a compact two-layer MLP in an ensemble architecture, where the tree provides fast-path classification and the MLP refines uncertain cases. Model weights are exported as Rust `const` arrays, enabling zero-allocation deployment with no runtime deserialization. We formalize structural safety properties of the ensemble in the Lean~4 theorem prover, establishing a three-tier verification approach covering structural invariants, weight-dependent decision bounds, and floating-point error propagation. In initial small-scale trials on a combined dataset of production logs, CSIC-2010, and CIC-IDS2017-derived features, the ensemble achieves >99% validation accuracy for both scanner and DDoS detection, with tree inference completing in under 2ns and full ensemble inference under 6ns. We discuss limitations of the current training data and outline directions for scaling to larger, human-labeled corpora.
items.title: Sub-Microsecond HTTP Threat Detection with Decision Tree–MLP Ensembles and Lean 4 Verification

items.summary: Privacy leakage in LLM agents is commonly evaluated within individual components such as memory, retrieval, or tool-use pipelines, which makes it difficult to distinguish internal exposure from information that an external observer can actually recover. We present CIPL (Channel Inversion for Privacy Leakage), a channel-aware evaluation framework for black-box privacy leakage in LLM agents. CIPL represents a target through sensitive source, selection, assembly, execution, observation, and extraction stages and evaluates the transition from selected sensitive units to attacker-recoverable output under a shared protocol. Experiments across memory-based, retrieval-mediated, and tool-mediated targets, together with a BrowserUse live-agent case study, show that storage labels alone do not determine recoverability. Memory targets form a near-saturated reference case, retrieval-mediated leakage is frequently partial, and tool-mediated and live-agent leakage varies strongly with observation surface, prompt-to-channel alignment, retrieval depth, and provider behavior. A stratified semantic audit further identifies attacker-useful disclosures that canonical exact matching misses. CIPL therefore provides a common framework for comparing how internal sensitive dependence is realized as externally recoverable leakage across heterogeneous agent pipelines.
items.title: CIPL: A Channel-Aware Framework for Recoverable Privacy Leakage in LLM Agents

items.summary: Solver, driver scripts and every numerical output of a study of the efficiency and the retrieved-mode noise of a Lambda-type atomic quantum memory. The model is the one-dimensional Maxwell-Bloch system of a three-level ensemble with the anti-Stokes four-wave-mixing channel, integrated in JAX/Diffrax so that the derivative of an observable with respect to the control field comes from a reverse pass through the propagation. The noise observable is one row of the Bogoliubov kernel projected on the retrieved temporal mode, obtained without assembling the kernel. The outputs cover: the efficiency-noise front traced over a 32-knot control at two signal detunings; the largest singular value of the storage-retrieval map along that front and its dependence on the four-wave-mixing coupling; the spin-wave growth of the resonant anti-Stokes configuration over 2.5 decades of optical depth and a factor 15 in control amplitude; the efficiency, noise photon number and collinear phase mismatch of a cesium configuration taken from published experimental parameters; the derivative of each front point with respect to the optical depth, the spin decoherence, the phase mismatch and the four-wave-mixing coupling, each from one reverse pass; three optimizers compared at one evaluation budget and at three control dimensions, with the cost of a gradient measured against the cost of an objective on the same working point; the number of temporal modes the storage map resolves, on a ladder in the basis size at two spatial grids; the Doppler-averaged absorption of a warm vapour in closed form; three velocity quadratures measured against that closed form and against its derivative, which is the average the field's source carries; the integrator step a velocity-resolved solve needs, which is not the step the front was traced at; the landed controls of the second detuning read again under a 300 K Maxwellian, at one velocity class and at thirty; the Bogoliubov identity projected on the retrieved mode, evaluated at every front point; the noise the detector gate collects over every temporal mode, by stochastic trace estimation, and the effective mode count it gives against the retrieved-mode count; the same trace against the gate's own length; a manifest of every landed run with its detuning, step specification, bound and outcome; the reproducibility of the front, measured as the disagreement between two runs of one control that reach the same efficiency, and what that reproducibility does to a slope read off the front; and the front re-traced at a constant integrator step over both searches, with the local logarithmic slope read on it at three efficiencies fixed before the set was read.  Every output file is plain text carrying its own configuration in a header and a machine-readable RESULT line; DEPOSIT.md maps the directories and names the script that produces each. The archive is a git archive of one commit, so the tree is exactly what that revision held.
items.title: Simulation outputs for a differentiable Maxwell-Bloch model of a Lambda-type atomic quantum memory with four-wave mixing

items.summary: Within the Complementarity-First and Reciprocal Internal Complementarity research program, we study regular perturbations of a supplied smooth massive degree-one SU(2) Yang–Mills–Higgs monopole with equal scalar and vector masses. A neutral transverse readout satisfies an exact nonlinear equation whose source is a divergence of an L2 tensor plus an L6/5 remainder. An additional affine infrared class is preserved on compact regular intervals and transported to admitted framed gauge and collective charts. Ordinary kinetic collective subtraction need not preserve its homogeneous negative norm; a compensating sum retains the relevant cancellation. Pure spatial transport is skew, while complete coordinate corrections admit an endpoint Duhamel identity. These statements concern finite-time admissibility, not uniform all-time localization. Assuming the companion’s nonnegative physical Hessian, complete framed kernel, local-moment coercivity and explicit threshold-packet estimates, a Gauss projection of a compact weighted translation yields a sharper test in the same monopole background. Its affine tail label differs from its actual initial local center rate, and its collective-orthogonal velocity lies outside the domain of the physical Hessian’s inverse square root. Its global linearized local-moment connection residual is unbounded in kinetic L2 while remaining bounded in the energy norm. We obtain an exponentially weighted time-average lower bound, not a universal pointwise growth law. Fixed-time differentiability excludes a time-uniform linear-scale nonlinear strong-residual estimate on this class, but does not establish nonlinear Lyapunov instability. The actual spectral inverse-square-root domain is necessary and sufficient for bounded unforced linear radiative position. We identify the nonlinear physical source that would need stronger control. The example proves that affine admissibility does not imply spectral admissibility; it does not classify their full inclusion relation or prove all-time nonlinear spectral propagation.
tags: Complementarity-First; Reciprocal Internal Complementarity; magnetic monopole; infrared control; affine tail class; spectral inverse domain; collective modulation; threshold wave; Lean.
items.title: Affine and Spectral Infrared Control of Monopole Perturbations

items.summary: Emergency department (ED) decision-making relies on heterogeneous clinical information, including patient history, vital signs, laboratory results, and electrocardiograms (ECGs). Vision--language models (VLMs) can jointly process these modalities, but strong predictive performance does not necessarily imply meaningful use of the correct patient's ECG. We term this failure mode ECG Mirage: apparent multimodal capability without useful dependence on patient-specific ECG information. We distinguish two forms: ECG neglect, where ECGs provide little predictive benefit, and ECG confusion, where matched ECGs outperform no-image inputs but not mismatched ECGs. To evaluate these behaviours, we compare predictions obtained with matched ECGs, outcome-discordant mismatched ECGs, and no-image inputs while holding the clinical text and prediction targets fixed. Across four VLMs on MDS-ED, matched ECGs provide no consistent advantage for either ICU admission or clinical deterioration prediction. We then train four restricted visual prompts using supervised learning followed by conditional direct preference optimisation, while keeping the VLM backbone frozen. The resulting models achieve balanced accuracies of 70.6% for ICU admission and 67.5% for deterioration and increase the matched-versus-mismatched performance gap to approximately 16.5 and 5.5 percentage points, respectively. Overall, our study identifies ECG Mirage in multimodal clinical prediction and introduces visual prompt tuning as an efficient mitigation strategy.
items.title: ECG Mirage: Revealing and Mitigating the Underutilisation of ECGs in Vision-Language Models for Clinical Prediction

items.summary: Abstract Distributed version control preserves source states, ancestry, branching, merging, and collaboration with extraordinary success. It does not ordinarily require engineering intent, failed approaches, claim scope, verification evidence, residual disagreement, or continuation state to exist as typed repository objects. Those records instead tend to be distributed across commit prose, review systems, issue trackers, CI logs, artifact stores, chat, and human memory. This disclosure explores a broader version-control model for software developed by humans and agents without claiming that content addressing, provenance, attestations, change-oriented versioning, or agent memory are new in isolation. Gemel models an evidence-bearing change : a content-addressed relation from an exact input state to an exact output state, linked to intent, operations, producer provenance, claims, evidence, residuals, verification scope, and causal context. Trajectories preserve completed, rejected, interrupted, superseded, and inconclusive work. Claims remain declarations rather than stored truth; support and readiness are derived conservatively from evidence, residuals, freshness, supersession, and policy. Context manifests and checkpoints provide bounded continuation surfaces without requiring private reasoning transcripts. The inspected Rust reference implementation defines deterministic canonical encoding, BLAKE3-256 identities, immutable objects, mutable refs, rebuildable indexes, 24 object families, Git-carried exchange, deterministic Git projection, semantic indexing, native and hosted synchronization, agent queries, policy checks, and an FRF court runner. For this paper, the supplied source archive was independently built in a clean temporary directory and cargo test --all-targets completed 236 tests with zero failures. This result is implementation-specific conformance evidence. It is not evidence that Gemel improves developer productivity, agent reliability, or industrial outcomes. Gemel composes with the Forensic Residual Framework (FRF) as an evidence plane and with FRF-Fuzz as a discovery plane. The paper situates that composition against Git facilities, patch algebra, provenance models, software-supply-chain attestations, reproducible builds, software archives, event sourcing, rationale capture, and agent memory. It discloses alternative embodiments and defines falsifiable evaluations for handoff quality, repeated-error reduction, evidence freshness, reconciliation, interoperability, context cost, storage overhead, and longitudinal fuzzing. Its principal claim is architectural: software history can be represented as an engineering graph in which source state, intent, evidence, residual uncertainty, negative knowledge, and continuation state possess explicit identity and scope. Whether that representation earns its operational cost remains an empirical question. Keywords distributed version control; Git; agentic software development; evidence engineering; provenance; content addressing; Merkle DAG; software agents; developmental trajectories; negative knowledge; residual primacy; FRF; FRF-Fuzz; reproducibility; software archaeology; semantic lineage; source provenance; event sourcing.
items.title: Gemel: Evidence-Native Version Control for Agentic Software Development - Longitudinal Engineering Memory, Residual-Aware Change Graphs, Git Interchange, and Reproducible Agent Handoffs

items.summary: Long-context large language model inference is increasingly limited by prefill, where dense self-attention processes the entire prompt before generation begins. Sparse block selection can reduce this cost, but a block centroid may hide a highly relevant token among many irrelevant ones. We call this failure mode mean dilution and propose RBS-Attention, a training-free sparse-prefill method with two complementary selection branches. A centroid base branch captures average relevance, while a rescue branch uses the maximum key-block radius and its prompt-, layer-, and head-dependent distribution to identify blocks at risk of underestimation. Independently thresholding the two branches and combining their masks controls the contribution of rescue blocks while preserving regular block-sparse FlashAttention execution. On H100 GPUs, RBS-Attention achieves 20.65$\times$ standalone prefill-attention speedup, 11.92$\times$ vLLM prefill-attention speedup, and 5.97$\times$ end-to-end time-to-first-token speedup at 128K on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8. On the dense Qwen3-32B model, it obtains 88.65 overall RULER accuracy versus 89.52 for dense attention; LongBench-v2, InfiniteBench, and Video-MME provide additional quality evaluation. Supporting experiments measure actual retention, compare selectors at matched density, and characterize block-size, threshold, and memory behavior. Together, these results support radius-adaptive dual-branch selection as an effective approach to long-context prefill.
items.title: RBS-Attention: Radius-Bounded Sparse Prefill for Long-Context Large Language Models

items.summary: This paper refines the finiteness conjecture for stability architectures and establishes the strongest currently provable results. A stability claim is treated as a profile specifying the object, state space, evolution, perturbation class, projection, failure region, time horizon, and obstructing gap or invariant. An architecture abstracts the structural core: the category of state spaces, the operator class, the gap functional, and the transport obstruction. The paper proves that stability cannot be classified from the trajectory map alone; the full profile matters. For linear systems, there are exactly three distinct architectures: dissipative, geometric or gradient, and Hamiltonian. For model-theoretic stability, the classification is finite and known: stability, NIP, simplicity, and rosiness. This logical classification is an analogy, not a direct translation to dynamics. For Hamiltonian systems, conditional finiteness identifies five candidate mechanisms: KAM persistence, Nekhoroshev confinement, Trojan resonance-gap suppression, symmetry constraint, and barrier obstruction. For statistical systems, four candidates appear: uniform, partial, and non-uniform hyperbolicity, plus rate conditions. In both cases, finiteness follows only if the lists are exhaustive, which remains conjectural. The paper also proves an intra-architecture transfer theorem, a qualified cross-architecture rigidity theorem, and a proposition on overlapping architectures. Transfer works within a shared architecture because estimates depend only on structural data. Rigidity blocks transfer between structurally distinct architectures unless additional structure exists. Overlap is possible, allowing multiple stability mechanisms and multiple failure routes. The general classification problem is undecidable, proved by reduction from the halting problem. Limitations include autonomous, finite-dimensional, smooth dynamics; time-dependent, infinite-dimensional, non-smooth, and nonlinear cases remain open. The consequences concern analog laboratories, engineering design by architecture selection, and a finite core of stability theory. The central message is that the finiteness conjecture is not vacuous: it holds where testable, while full generality awaits resolution of the exhaustiveness conjectures.
items.title: Stability Architectures: A Finite Classification of Provable Cases

items.summary: This paper asks a narrow question. Lyapunov stability, geometric stability, and statistical stability are all described as spectral-gap properties. The gaps act on different operators, live on different spaces, and survive different perturbations. The informal habit of treating them as one nested hierarchy is correct for convex wells and hyperbolic sinks. It is not correct as a statement about dynamical systems in general. The paper replaces that habit with a comparison theorem. A stability claim is a profile: an evolution, a perturbation class, a projection, and a failure set. Comparative type can change when the map is held fixed and only the projection changes. Three statistical properties are kept distinct. The first is weak continuity of an invariant measure under perturbation. The second is a spectral gap of a transfer or Fokker–Planck operator on a named function space. The third is differentiability of the measure in the perturbation parameter. These three can hold together. They can also separate. The proved implications are scoped. A positive Hessian implies Lyapunov stability of a mechanical equilibrium and a dissipative Jacobian gap for a gradient flow. A hyperbolic sink gives weak continuity of a Dirac family and does not give mixing on a positive-dimensional density space. Uniform hyperbolicity gives a transfer-operator gap on an anisotropic space and, in the perturbation class of Keller and Liverani, weak continuity of an SRB family. Partial hyperbolicity yields a gap only after restriction to the hyperbolic factor. Nonuniform hyperbolicity with a Young tower yields a slower, tail-controlled rate and is compatible with instability of almost every orbit. A prescribed decay for a piecewise expanding map or a hypocoercive generator need not come from any hyperbolic splitting. Architectural estimates do not transfer between structurally distinct operator classes. In one linear-quadratic noise model the three classical tests return the same number. In a double well they separate. The paper does not claim that statistical mechanisms are finite, and it does not prove that averaging a frequency-gap Hamiltonian system produces a kinetic spectral gap.
items.title: Which Spectral Gaps Imply Which: Lyapunov, Geometric, and Statistical Criteria

items.summary: Memory segmentation is thought to arise from rapid decorrelation in neural activity, often quantified by Euclidean distance or cosine angle. Although these metrics detect a transition, they do not reveal how the new state relates to the repertoire represented by the neural manifold. This matters because neuromodulators that drive state transitions also alter excitability, and learning may repurpose existing representations or create new ones. Here, I introduce a geometric decomposition that separates changes attributable to gain modulation of a nearby manifold state from movement within the manifold and genuine off-manifold displacement. The approach uses the radial axis of neural population activity to partition the normal space of a local manifold region. A central challenge is identifiability: given only a static reference manifold and a single test state, neither the state from which a perturbation began nor its gain magnitude and mechanistic decomposition can generally be recovered uniquely. I therefore formulate identifiability as a cascade of geometric gates specifying when each component can be interpreted. The gates distinguish structural failures, including the absence of a local chart or incorrect intrinsic dimensionality, from estimation error and systematic bias caused by reference sampling, tangent-frame error, gain-axis misalignment, anchor displacement, and poor ratio conditioning. Simulations show that neighborhood size, curvature, sampling density, ambient dimension, and noise act through a small set of geometric quantities. The framework specifies when assignments to gain or novelty are identifiable, how they become biased, and which diagnostics reveal the relevant failure regime. By quantifying the nature rather than only the magnitude of neural state change, it provides a clear, readily interpretable framework for evaluating mechanisms of neural state transitions.
items.title: Identifying Neural State Changes due to Gain versus Off-Manifold Displacement

items.summary: Behavioral failures can make a transformer appear to lack a world model even when it has learned faithful representations of its environment. We demonstrate this in TaxiGPT, a transformer trained on random walks through Manhattan whose failures have been interpreted as evidence of an incoherent internal map. Through mechanistic analysis and causal interventions, we show that the model represents intersections and streets, tracks its position, and uses a goal compass to navigate. We trace its failures to interference between superposed intersection features, which disrupts localization within the internal map. Affordance packing, which groups representations of intersections with the same legal moves, helps limit the consequences of these errors. Finally, we propose mechanistic indicators that we use to compare models and show that world-modeling capacities emerge at different stages of training. Our findings motivate a shift from asking whether a model has a world model to mechanistically studying its world modeling: the interacting capacities through which it represents its environment and uses those representations to guide behavior.
items.title: World Modeling in Transformers

items.summary: When language models reason in chain-of-thought or exchange free-text intermediates, they serialize structured information into natural language. How much tree-structured compositional content survives this bottleneck? We propose a round-trip protocol that answers this question empirically for tree-structured expressions. A generator converts a procedurally generated arithmetic expression into a word problem, a separate extractor recovers the expression from the word problem alone, and symbolic equivalence provides an exact oracle. Evaluating all pairwise combinations of sixteen models yields a communication matrix whose marginals separate generation quality from extraction quality. Three main findings emerge. First, the channel is lossy and asymmetric: swapping which model generates and which extracts shifts accuracy by up to 60.4 points, and the best pair reaches 92.9% by combining different models on each end rather than the same model on both. Second, at least 73.6% of round-trip failures originate at generation, and difficulty is driven by tree structure (operator count, depth, right-branching) rather than model family. Third, the channel is trainable: ~3600 fine-tuning examples that share the evaluation's operators and tree shapes lift every open-weight model above untrained Gemini-3.1-Pro, an upper bound under matched semantics. A disjoint-domain regime with new operators and vocabulary also raises every open-weight model, confirming the gain is not an artifact of matched semantics, though a gap to the frontier remains. Together these results identify tree-structured expression serialization as a primary limiting factor when models communicate hierarchical structure through natural language.
items.title: The Communication Bottleneck: A Round-Trip Study of Tree-Structured Expression Serialization in Language Models

items.summary: Robot demonstration collection often produces imperfect or failed trajectories in addition to successful demonstrations. Existing methods typically exploit failed trajectories by identifying segments that still make progress toward task completion, but largely overlook \textit{failure-critical behaviors} that directly lead to task failure. Here we argue that these two types of segments provide fundamentally asymmetric supervision: progressive segments should be imitated, whereas failure-critical segments should be explicitly avoided. Based on this observation, we propose CARF, a Contrastive Attraction-Repulsion of Failure-guided framework for learning from imperfect robot data. CARF introduces a progress-based importance scorer, trained solely on successful expert demonstrations and its perturbation results, to estimate step-wise contributions toward task completion and identify informative regions in failed trajectories. These scores guide a unified flow-matching objective that attracts the policy toward progressive behaviors and repels it from failure-critical ones, while excluding ambiguous segments. This enables more comprehensive utilization of imperfect data and avoids unreliable supervision from ambiguous failure segments. Extensive experiments in simulation and the real world demonstrate consistent improvements over competing baselines across diverse failure scenarios, with ablations further validating the effectiveness of the proposed scoring and attraction-repulsion mechanisms. Our website is https://zhao-sq.github.io/carf/#.
items.title: CARF: Contrastive Attraction-Repulsion of Failure-Guided Flow Matching

items.summary: Graph-enhanced multi-agent systems (G-MAS) coordinate large language model agents through communication graphs and role assignments, which determine how agents exchange information and divide responsibilities. However, final-score comparisons across systems combine differences in models, communication patterns, roles, and computation costs, making performance differences difficult to attribute to specific communication structures, role assignments, and information flows. To address this evaluation attribution problem, we introduce OpenMAS-GCom, a benchmark for diagnosing how these components affect G-MAS performance through controlled interventions. We represent systems through collaboration units, communication links, shared intermediate information, and execution rules. OpenMAS-GCom compares original systems with versions modified by changing one component while keeping tasks, models, prompts, and budget limits fixed. We rewire communication edges, remove specialist or critic agents, replace intermediate messages with incorrect content, and disable workers during execution. The benchmark evaluates 17 single-agent, ordinary multi-agent, and graph-enhanced configurations on 29 datasets across six domains. We add 400 G-MAS-Complex tasks requiring agents to combine information from multiple documents, resolve conflicting records, and return specified values with source identifiers. Experiments show larger mean losses after specialist removal than after critic removal, different performance degradation under incorrect messages and worker failures despite similar original scores, and different configurations achieving the highest accuracy and accuracy per token on G-MAS-Complex.
items.title: OpenMAS-GCom. A Diagnostic Benchmark for Graph-enhanced Multi-Agent Systems

items.summary: Reproducibility release 1.1.0 for Ocean Engineering manuscript OE-D-25-10458. This package supports a controlled Rotterdam-Yokohama comparison of the Suez, Cape and Northern Sea Route corridors using three predefined strategic waypoint philosophies per corridor. The archive contains the Python routing and analysis code, all nine waypoint definitions, frozen maritime-network geometries and scenario/leg distances, dual-coastline quality-assurance and local-repair reports, 0.05/0.025-degree convergence outputs, sourced OpenStreetMap Suez Canal geometry and provenance, downstream time/fuel/CO2 analyses, exponent and vessel-reference sensitivities, and the frozen manuscript sources and figures. The routing method uses searoute 1.4.3, WGS84 distance recomputation and no great-circle fallback. The reproduction command stages the archived routes, regenerates downstream tables and copies the included figure assets. A full routing rerun additionally requires the externally distributed Natural Earth 10 m v5.1.1 and GSHHG 2.3.7 full L1 coastline datasets. Tests and release checks are documented in the archive. The comparison is strategic and does not predict realised voyages or commercial viability.
items.title: Effects of Route Representation on Distance and Downstream Voyage Implications in Europe–Asia Trade: A Comparison of the Suez, Cape, and Northern Sea Route Corridors

items.summary: This record contains replication materials for “AI-intensive scientific collaboration exposes unequal coverage in name-based bibliometrics” by Anirban Adhikary and Sourav Bikash Borah. The archive contains the public analysis code, environment specifications, documentation, public-safe aggregate materials, frozen reference outputs, figure sources, and verification tools associated with the study. The public archive reproduces and verifies results within the documented derived-input boundary. It does not redistribute the approximately 770 GB OpenAlex source snapshot. Certain author-level derived inputs, including identifier-bearing bibliometric, name, affiliation, and network records, are excluded from public release because their combination creates a material reidentification risk. Full controlled reproduction requiring these inputs is available subject to an approved research purpose, identity verification, appropriate data-use conditions, and applicable third-party restrictions. The archive documents the analytical workflow, software environment, input contracts, cryptographic hashes, output lineage, and the distinction between public verification and controlled-input execution. The reported analyses are associational.
items.title: Replication package for "AI-intensive scientific collaboration exposes unequal coverage in name-based bibliometrics"

items.summary: This release contains the SMT-LIB2 benchmarks accompanying our paper, "Invulnerability Checking for Memory Protection Extensions Against Meltdown." It includes 16 benchmarks covering load-store queue sizes of 8, 16, 32, and 64 entries. Each size includes a secure baseline and three MPX Trojan variants: Base, Bound, and Illegal Memory Access. A verification script runs the benchmarks using Z3, checks the results against the expected outcomes, and saves the solver output and execution times.
items.title: Supporting Code for Invulnerability Checking for Memory Protection Extensions Against Meltdown

items.summary: Self-contained synthetic seismic–gravity inversion models, Python operators, seeds, archived and profile-initialized fits, regional controls, posterior samples, figures and validation records for the manuscript by Emilson P. Leite and Maiara M. Gonçalves. Version 0.11 adds a four-start calibration on 96 paired noise comparisons, an audit of unchanged displayed seismic median errors, exact n=32 coverage intervals, and empirical bias–variance accounting of the existing regional controls. The four-start shortcut did not reproduce the profile solutions; the manuscript retains 32 profile-initialized noise pairs for each free-geometry configuration. Fixed-geometry ensembles retain 256 realizations. Wide local intervals under a free trend coexist with systematic target-property errors directed towards the prior. No new posterior chains were generated in this revision. Field observations and third-party BP-model data are not required.
items.title: When gravity adds useful information to interpretation-conditioned post-stack seismic inversion: reproducibility archive

items.summary: Discovering the structure and kinetics of chemical reaction networks (CRNs) from time-series concentration data is a fundamental challenge in chemical kinetics, with existing approaches relying on prior mechanistic assumptions or suffering from high computational cost and noise sensitivity. In this work, we present integral chemical reaction neural networks (iCRNNs), a framework that combines the interpretable, physics-constrained, architecture of chemical reaction neural networks (CRNNs) with an integral collocation formulation of the governing dynamics. Rather than solving ODEs forward in time at each training step, we approximate the integral of the learned rate functions directly using numerical quadrature. This yields an entirely algebraic forward pass consisting only of matrix operations, eliminating the repeated adaptive ODE solves of standard CRNN and producing smoother, more predictable training. We provide a recovery error analysis characterising the structural sources of ill-conditioning (conservation laws, reaction reversibility, and shared reactant sets) that limit network identifiability. On two benchmark CRNs, iCRNN trains in roughly half the wall-clock time of the baseline CRNN method on a four-species mechanism and between three and four times faster on a five-species mechanism, while completing every training run reliably and attaining comparable or lower loss.
items.title: Integral chemical reaction neural networks

items.summary: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) are highly sensitive to label noise, since corrupted supervision can propagate through the graph and degrade learned node representations. This work proposes PCC+GCN, a hybrid framework that uses Particle Competition and Cooperation (PCC) as a graph-based label-refinement stage before GCN training. PCC identifies suspicious labeled nodes through particle domination dynamics and determines whether their labels should be preserved, removed, or reassigned before GCN training. The framework also allows the graph used by PCC to be augmented with feature-based $k$-nearest-neighbor edges, while the GCN itself is trained on the original graph structure and node features. The proposed method was evaluated on ten graph datasets from the NoisyGL benchmark under conventional Uniform, Pair, and Random label noise, as well as under instance-dependent label noise. A detailed hyperparameter analysis was also conducted on Cora, CiteSeer, and PubMed. Under conventional noise, PCC+GCN achieved the highest overall average accuracy and the best average rank among the evaluated methods, with an average gain of $1.67$ percentage points over the baseline GCN across the clean setting and all noisy scenarios. Under instance-dependent noise, PCC+GCN remained competitive with the best-performing robust methods while requiring substantially lower execution time, being the fastest robust method on eight of the ten datasets. The results indicate that PCC-based label refinement provides an effective and computationally efficient preprocessing strategy for improving GCN robustness under noisy supervision.
items.title: Particle Competition and Cooperation for Robust Graph Convolutional Network Learning Under Label Noise

items.summary: Long-term memory is essential for large language model (LLM) agents to maintain consistency and personalization over extended interactions. Existing memory systems typically rely on fixed granularities or static schemas, but these designs struggle when heterogeneous information, such as preferences, events, constraints, and temporal updates, is embedded in a single mixed representation. The resulting semantic interference makes top-K retrieval sensitive to noise and often leaves relevant evidence poorly ranked. We present AutoViewMem, a data-driven framework that organizes long-term conversational memory into self-configuring, low-overlap semantic views before indexing. AutoViewMem discovers candidate views from interaction traces, selects a compact complementary view set, and uses these views to guide write-time structured extraction of provenance-grounded memories. This representation-first design moves semantic disentanglement from retrieval time to write time, allowing standard top-K similarity search to retrieve focused evidence without explicit routing or iterative retrieval. We further apply offline consolidation to improve memory compactness and consistency. Experiments on the LoCoMo and PersonaMem benchmarks, under both Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B backbones, show that AutoViewMem improves long-horizon question answering and personalization over strong memory baselines while preserving a simple inference pipeline.
items.title: AutoViewMem: Self-Configuring Orthogonal Views for Conversational Long-Term Memory

items.summary: Traditional unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) methods are designed to flag or localise deviations from a normative distribution, ignoring the underlying generative mechanisms of the anomalies. Yet the nature of an anomaly is often as important as its presence. We reformulate UAD as a Bayesian inverse problem, in which the objective is to infer the most probable corruption responsible for each observation. Our framework yields a probabilistic anomaly score as the energy of the inferred corruption parameters, and serves as a principled recipe for developing new UAD algorithms. We derive several existing methods as instances of the general framework, each corresponding to the same energy score under different modelling choices. Experimentally, we study the framework's components in a controlled setting, and improve object-class AUROC on the MVTec AD dataset by 2.3% by adapting the underlying corruption model. Finally, we validate the framework on a brain MRI benchmark, achieving strong detection performance while producing estimates of pathology intensity, bias, and geometry. Code is available at https://github.com/jgmyles/inverse-uad.
items.title: A Principled Approach to Unsupervised Anomaly Detection

items.summary: Supporting material for the manuscript "Subacute oral glyphosate impairs testicular function in male mice (Mus musculus): a threshold-anchored dose-response study of steroidogenesis, sperm quality, redox balance and spermatogenic histopathology" (Elbeeh, Filfilan, Filfilan and Filfilan), submitted to Drug and Chemical Toxicology (Taylor & Francis). Forty adult male Swiss albino (ICR) mice, 8-10 weeks old and 22.1-25.5 g at allocation, received vehicle (distilled water) or technical-grade glyphosate at 10, 50 or 100 mg/kg/day by oral gavage for 28 days, n = 10 per group. The dose range brackets the regulatory no-observed-adverse-effect level of approximately 50 mg/kg/day. Endpoints measured in the same 40 animals: body and testis weight; serum testosterone, LH and FSH; epididymal sperm concentration, progressive motility, viability and morphology; testicular malondialdehyde, reduced glutathione, superoxide dismutase and catalase; and testis histopathology stained with haematoxylin-eosin and with periodic acid-Schiff, assessed by the Johnsen tubular-maturation score and by measurement of seminiferous tubule diameter, germinal epithelial height and graded lesion severity. Sections were digitised on a Philips UltraFast Scanner at the x20 level (0.5 micrometres per pixel) and reviewed in the Philips PathologySuite viewer; morphometry was performed in ImageJ v1.54 with semi-automated annotation in QuPath v0.4.3 on fields exported at the native scan resolution. Contents: S1, the manufacturer's Certificate of Analysis for the test article (Sigma-Aldrich 337757, lot MKCZ1523, purity at least 96 per cent, CAS 1071-83-6); S2, analytical kits, instruments, assay conditions and intra- and inter-assay coefficients of variation; S3, the analysis and figure-plotting code; S4, the complete per-animal dataset underlying every figure and table; S5, the benchmark-dose model set with BMD and BMDL10 values; and Supplementary Figure S6 with its caption, showing the histomorphometry and graded lesion scores of Table 4 with individual animal values overlaid. README.md gives the full manifest. Every value reported in the manuscript can be recomputed from S4 using the code in S3. Statistics: continuous endpoints were compared by Welch's ANOVA with the Games-Howell post-hoc test; ordinal lesion grades by the Kruskal-Wallis test with Holm-adjusted Dunn's post-hoc test; monotonic trend by the Jonckheere-Terpstra test; and the endpoint family was controlled at a false-discovery rate of 5 per cent (Benjamini-Hochberg). The Johnsen tubular-maturation score was nominated in advance as the primary endpoint; every other endpoint is secondary. Ethics: all procedures were approved by the Bioethics Committee of Umm Al-Qura University, Makkah, Saudi Arabia (approval no. HAPO-02-K-012-2025-04-2781) and were conducted in accordance with the ARRIVE 2.0 guidelines. These 40 animals also support the cardiotoxicity, neurotoxicity and immunotoxicity arms of the same programme, which are reported separately under the same approval number. Licensed CC BY 4.0.
items.title: Supplementary data and analysis code for: Subacute oral glyphosate impairs testicular function in male mice (Mus musculus)

items.summary: Multi-agent active inference gives a natural account of belief sharing: agents hold local posteriors over a shared latent state, communicate those beliefs, and pool them into a colony-level consensus. The same mechanism is fragile when a member is miscalibrated, corrupted, or strategically wrong. Because the standard pool multiplies the reports together, a single confident-but-wrong broadcast that puts near-zero mass on the true state can pull the whole consensus off it, outweighing many honest members. The colony therefore needs a way to preserve the useful structure of belief sharing while limiting the influence of contaminated beliefs. This paper presents Active Fedference, a discrete-categorical framework that connects robust federated generalized variational inference with active inference belief sharing. The main bridge is structural: standard belief sharing appears as the non-robust corner of a broader generalized-Bayes family, while robust losses, conservative server fusion, and explicit aggregation diagnostics describe how the system moves away from that corner under declared contamination mechanisms. The result is not a replacement for belief sharing, but a containment result: ordinary belief sharing is recovered when robustness is turned off. Bounded-loss theory applies on the client axis, while the variational-server axis supplies an objective-backed redescending weight update. Following the manuscript's authoritative three-axis guarantee map, the paper keeps source-conditional client updates, a recovery-only heuristic server rule, and an objective-backed variational server rule as separate claim owners, with no robustness guarantee transferred between them. The study suite then exercises the framework as an end-to-end research system: recovery checks anchor the standard-Bayes limit, belief-sharing studies verify the communication baseline, contamination experiments test robust consensus, and extension studies probe moving agents, hierarchical latent structure, sensitivity to acuity and colony size, parameter recovery, and single-host socket-backed federation traces. All reported quantities are generated from deterministic analysis artifacts and injected into the manuscript by token, so the paper, figures, release package, and validation reports remain tied to the same execution record. The open-source repository is ActiveInferenceInstitute/Active_Fedference. This final-release manuscript uses assigned version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22149133; the bound deposited PDF and repository release are controlled by separate publication gates.
items.title: Robust Belief Sharing in Federated Active Inference: A Recovery-Tested Generalized-Variational Framework for Categorical Contamination-Aware Consensus

items.summary: Replication data and code for a study of hedge-ratio estimation (OLS, DCC-GARCH, Random Forest, XGBoost and a naïve benchmark) for CME Bitcoin and Ether futures under regime-dependent tail risk. The package contains date-aligned daily returns and hedge-ratio series (BTC: 19 December 2017 to 22 May 2025; ETH: 8 February 2021 to 22 May 2025), Python scripts that reproduce all tables and figures, and a README. Raw Yahoo Finance prices are not redistributed. This version corrects the construction of returns (spot and futures returns are measured between the same CME trading dates) and supersedes any earlier deposit.
items.title: Replication data and code: hedge ratios for cryptocurrency futures under regime-dependent tail risk

items.summary: As LLM capabilities have expanded, multi-agent communication has emerged as an increasingly active area of research. Prevailing protocols often adopt rigid structures that introduce coordination bottlenecks and can degrade as the number of agents increases. We introduce Proxifield, a round-adaptive multi-agent protocol with decentralized agent decision-making that constructs sparse communication graphs from the evolving semantic proximity of agents. Without model training or a centralized planner, Proxifield connects agents using four routing signals derived at inference time: direct address, information needs, plan alignment, and information complementarity. We compare Proxifield with two representative coordination baselines, a centralized Star protocol and a decentralized Shared Context protocol, across two domains: Drone Search and Rescue and the collective-reasoning benchmark HiddenBench. We first ablate base-model capability and find that, in both domains, the performance of Proxifield improves with model size (35B -> 397B parameter model) and Proxifield outperforms all baselines at the largest scale. As team size increases, Proxifield's task-reward advantage over Star widens from 5.4% at (N=5) to 53.0% at (N=25) and 59.5% at (N=50), while Shared Context consistently underperforms both protocols. Proxifield is also substantially more robust to permanent agent failure, retaining 73.6% of its no-failure task reward under the most severe condition, compared with 58.3% for Shared Context and 38.8% for Star. These results demonstrate that decentralized, semantically adaptive routing can improve the scalability and fault tolerance of multi-agent systems.
items.title: Proxifield: Decentralized Multi-Agent Communication through Semantic Proximity
